title: The Regiment of Valparaíso
premise: In 1918 Valparaíso, Theo Underhill delivers letters for the suffragist widow Mariana Fuentes, reading each one before it leaves his hands — a habit born of a war he never fought and a name he borrowed from a dead man. When a stranger arrives bearing letters in the handwriting of Captain Elias Underhill, officially killed at Gallipoli, Theo's carefully constructed identity begins to unravel: either the captain lives, or someone is forging his way into Theo's inheritance of secrets. As armistice negotiations stall and the naval workshop where Theo hides his work faces demolition orders, he races to finish restoring the captain's confiscated papers — evidence that could clear a executed deserter, implicate a Chilean admiral, or destroy Mariana's movement. In the end, Theo learns the handwriting is real: Elias survived, disfigured and amnesiac, and has been writing to find himself; Theo must choose between remaining invisible and claiming the brotherhood — and the burden — of a shared name.
about_author: W. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in Chilean port cities. The Regiment of Valparaíso is their second novel, following a well-received debut about lighthouse keepers on the Strait of Magellan.

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Words
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We meet him sealing, reading, and re-sealing Mariana Fuentes' correspondence in her hillside house above Valparaíso harbor. He catalogs the town's secrets in a mental ledger, believing invisibility is safety. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; the reader senses a man rehearsing a life rather than living one.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Funicular
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A gaunt stranger named Aldous Renn asks Theo to deliver a letter addressed to a dead man — Captain Elias Underhill. The handwriting stops Theo cold: it matches letters he has carried for years, letters he answered himself. Emotional beat: vertigo; the first crack in Theo's carefully maintained anonymity.

chapters.title: What the Widow Keeps Locked
chapters.summary: Mariana's POV. Mariana observes Theo's distraction and recalls how she found him five years ago, half-starved, carrying a satchel of a dead officer's papers she was supposed to burn. She kept both the papers and the boy. Emotional beat: maternal guilt entwined with political calculation.

chapters.title: The Workshop Below the Cliffs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo works nights in a condemned naval workshop restoring water-damaged documents — the captain's field reports implicating Admiral Delacroix in a deserter's execution. News arrives: demolition is moved up to before the armistice signing. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Letters to a Corpse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, intercut with letter excerpts. Flashback reveals Theo began answering letters meant for Elias after the death notice, inventing replies to comfort the captain's fiancée — then couldn't stop. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into fraud; Theo confronts how much of 'Elias Underhill' he has become.

chapters.title: Renn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn reveals he was the captain's batman and claims Elias wrote to him last month — from nowhere Theo can trace. He offers Theo proof of the captain's survival in exchange for the workshop papers. Emotional beat: suspicion; Renn knows too much about Theo's habits, suggesting surveillance or worse.

chapters.title: The Suffragist's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mariana's POV. Mariana weighs using the admiral scandal as leverage for the vote versus protecting Theo, whom she has come to love as a son. A raid on a sister chapter warns her the navy is hunting the papers too. Emotional beat: the cost of principle measured in people.

chapters.title: Ink That Refuses to Dry
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Forensic detail: the new letters are written on paper milled after Gallipoli, yet the hand is unmistakably Elias's — Theo taught himself to imitate it, so he alone can spot the difference between imitation and origin. Someone else learned the same hand. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition; grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Deserter's Daughter
chapters.summary: New character POV: Lucía, daughter of the executed deserter, arrives seeking the papers that would restore her father's name. She mistakes Theo for the captain himself. Emotional beat: Theo, wearing another man's history, receives gratitude meant for a ghost — shame and temptation in one embrace.

chapters.title: Admiral Delacroix's Tea
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Summoned to the naval headquarters under pretense of a delivery, Theo is interviewed by Delacroix, who quotes phrases from Theo's forged letters back at him. The admiral knows someone has been impersonating a dead officer. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse terror; Theo lies brilliantly and barely survives.

chapters.title: Mariana's Arrest Warrant
chapters.summary: Mariana's POV. Authorities move against the suffragist network, using the document scandal as pretext. Mariana burns her own archives but hides the workshop's location even from Theo, testing whether he trusts her. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as protection; two keepers of secrets circling each other.

chapters.title: The Hand in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Practicing Elias's handwriting to forge an alibi document, Theo realizes mid-stroke that he no longer knows which memories are his own — a childhood in Coquimbo, or one he absorbed from the captain's letters. Emotional beat: identity crisis at its deepest; the theme of inheritance made literal.

chapters.title: Renn Confesses, Partly
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn admits he has been forging the letters — paid by someone inside the admiralty to lure the papers out. But he swears the final letter, the one still undelivered, came to him genuinely. Emotional beat: unreliable ally; the mystery tightens instead of loosening.

chapters.title: Lucía's Vigil
chapters.summary: Lucía's POV. Lucía stakes out the workshop, having deduced its location from Theo's ink-stained cuffs. She witnesses navy clerks loading crates at night and must decide whether to warn the man she believes wronged her father. Emotional beat: vengeance deferred by dawning doubt.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Telegraphs hint the war may end within days — meaning the workshop falls with it. Theo races to finish restoration while Mariana, released on bond, sends coded warnings through the letter network he built. Emotional beat: the machinery of his double life finally serving a purpose larger than hiding.

chapters.title: The Night of the Crates
chapters.summary: Theo, Lucía, and Renn converge on the workshop as navy men haul out the restored documents. A fire starts — ambiguous, perhaps deliberate. Theo saves the deserter file but loses the captain's personal letters. Emotional beat: sacrifice; first open alliance between the three outsiders.

chapters.title: What Burned and What Didn't
chapters.summary: Mariana's POV. Mariana shelters the fugitives and reads the salvaged file: proof enough to ruin Delacroix, but only if delivered through channels the navy doesn't control — her movement's women couriers. Emotional beat: the private archive becomes a public weapon; Theo's secrecy ends.

chapters.title: Delacroix's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Delacroix offers Theo full pardon and a new identity abroad if he surrenders the file and names Mariana. Theo, offered exactly the invisibility he always wanted, refuses. Emotional beat: climax of character; the man who hid chooses exposure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wrote Himself Back
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The undelivered final letter leads them to a convalescent hospice outside Santiago: Elias Underhill, face scarred, memory shattered, has been writing letters to reconstruct a self — unknowingly competing with Theo's forgery of him. The two men meet. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; the corpse is alive and a stranger.

chapters.title: Two Men, One Name
chapters.summary: Alternating Theo/Elias POV. Over three days they trade memories, sorting which belong to whom. Elias, unable to testify coherently, authorizes Theo to speak in his name — legally, this time. Emotional beat: identity as something given, not clutched; brotherhood without blood.

chapters.title: The Reading of the File
chapters.summary: Mariana's POV. Before a packed courthouse and press, Theo reads the deserter file aloud in Elias's name while Mariana's couriers distribute copies citywide, making suppression impossible. Delacroix resigns rather than face court-martial. Emotional beat: catharsis; private papers become public truth, Lucía's father restored.

chapters.title: After the Signing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Armistice signed; the workshop is spared as a memorial archive Theo will run. He signs his own name — Theo Underhill, chosen, not borrowed — to the first letter he writes as himself, to Lucía. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance reclaimed as identity freely assumed.
